questions.q: Which of these gives the best idea of a point?
questions.a: The pointed end of a needle
o: The pointed end of a needle
A crease in a folded sheet of paper
The edge of a ruler
A beam of light from a torch

questions.q: A clothesline is stretched tight between two hooks, H and K, on opposite walls of a verandah. Which figure does the tight clothesline between the two hooks model?
questions.a: The line segment HK, with end points H and K
o: The line segment HK, with end points H and K
The line HK, going on endlessly beyond both hooks
The ray HK, starting at H and going on endlessly
The point H, because the clothesline starts there

questions.q:
Consider these statements.
I. A line segment includes both of its end points.
II. The line PQ can be measured with a ruler because it passes through P and Q.
III. Exactly one line can be drawn through two given points.
Which of these statements are correct?
questions.a: I and III only
o: I and III only
I and II only
II and III only
All three

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A dot made with a sharper pencil tip gives a better idea of a point than a dot made with a blunt tip.
Reason (R): A point marks a precise location but has no length, breadth or height.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: (a) What is a line segment? (b) Give one example from your classroom that gives the idea of a line segment.
questions.a: (a) A line segment is the shortest path between two points, including the two points, which are its end points. (b) For example, the edge of a desk, or the crease made by folding a sheet of paper and opening it.
s: (a) Says it is the shortest path between two points, including the two end points
(b) Gives a fitting example, such as the edge of a desk or a fold crease

questions.q: True or False: The line segment joining the points M and N can be written as MN or as NM. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. A line segment is named by its two end points in either order, so MN and NM are the same segment, with end points M and N.
s: States True
Gives the reason: a segment is named by its two end points, in either order

questions.q: Answer each part in one line. (a) How is a point usually named? (b) How many end points does a line segment have? (c) How many end points does a line have, and why?
questions.a: (a) By a single capital letter, such as P. (b) Two. (c) None, because a line extends endlessly in both directions.
s: (a) Says a point is named by a single capital letter
(b) States that a line segment has two end points
(c) States that a line has no end points because it extends endlessly both ways

questions.q: Points R, S, T and U lie on a straight line m, in that order. (a) Write any three different two-letter names for the line m. (b) Kavya says that line RU and line ST are two different lines because they use different points. Is she right? Give a reason. (c) Are the line segments RU and ST the same? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) Any three of RS, RT, RU, ST, SU and TU, for example RS, ST and TU. (b) No. All four points lie on the one line m, and two points determine a unique line, so RU and ST both name the line m. (c) No. Segment RU has end points R and U, while segment ST has end points S and T, so ST is only a part of RU.
s: (a) Gives three correct two-letter names for the line m
(b) Says Kavya is wrong, using the idea that two points determine a unique line
(c) Says the segments are different because their end points are different

questions.q: Five mobile towers P, Q, R, S and T stand in a district, and no three of them are on one straight line. A straight cable is to be laid between every pair of towers. (a) How many cables start from tower P? Name them. (b) Ravi says the total number of cables is 5 x 4 = 20. Explain the mistake in his count. (c) Find the correct total number of cables. (d) A sixth tower U is added, again not on a straight line with any two of the others. How many new cables are needed? (e) Find the total number of cables for the six towers.
questions.a: (a) 4 cables: PQ, PR, PS and PT. (b) Each cable joins two towers, so in 5 x 4 every cable is counted twice; for example PQ and QP are the same segment. (c) 20 / 2 = 10 cables. (d) 5 new cables: UP, UQ, UR, US and UT. (e) 10 + 5 = 15 cables.
s: (a) Finds 4 cables from P and names PQ, PR, PS, PT
(b) Explains that each cable is counted twice because PQ and QP are the same segment
(c) Finds the total 20 / 2 = 10
(d) Finds 5 new cables from U
(e) Finds the new total 10 + 5 = 15

questions.q:
For the school sports day, the groundsman fixes a flag at point A and another flag at point B, 60 m apart, on a flat field. He stretches a rope tightly from A to B and sprinkles lime powder along it to mark the straight finishing track. Later, a third flag C is fixed 20 m beyond B, on the same straight line as A and B, for the relay hand-over.
(a) What geometric figure does the lime mark from A to B model?
(b) Find the length of the line segment AC.
(c) The students imagine the lime mark carried on endlessly beyond A and beyond C. What figure would that be?
(d) How many line segments have two of the flags A, B and C as their end points? Name them.
questions.a: (a) The line segment AB, with end points A and B. (b) AC = 60 m + 20 m = 80 m. (c) A line (the line AC, which is the same as the line AB), extending endlessly in both directions. (d) Three: AB, BC and AC.
s: (a) Names the line segment AB
(b) Finds AC = 80 m
(c) Says it would be a line, extending endlessly both ways
(d) Names the three segments AB, BC and AC

questions.q: Which of these gives the idea of a ray?
questions.a: The beam from a lighthouse lamp going out to sea
o: The beam from a lighthouse lamp going out to sea
A string stretched tight between two nails
The sharpened tip of a pencil on paper
A straight road imagined endless both ways

questions.q: For the angle LMN, which of these correctly names its vertex and its arms?
questions.a: Vertex M; arms ML and MN
o: Vertex M; arms ML and MN
Vertex L; arms LM and LN
Vertex N; arms NL and NM
Vertex M; arms LM and NL

questions.q:
Match each item in Column I with the correct entry in Column II.
Column I: 1. The starting point of ray GH  2. The middle letter in the angle XYZ  3. The rays YX and YZ of the angle XYZ  4. The symbol that can replace the word 'angle'
Column II: A. the arms  B. ∠  C. G  D. the vertex

Assertion (A): ∠ABC and ∠BAC are two names for the same angle.
Reason (R): When an angle is named with three letters, the vertex is always written as the middle letter.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: (a) What is a ray? (b) Give one example from daily life that gives the idea of a ray.
questions.a: (a) A ray is a portion of a line that starts at one point, its starting point, and goes on endlessly in one direction. (b) For example, the light from a torch, or the sun's rays.
s: (a) Says a ray starts at one point and goes on endlessly in one direction
(b) Gives a fitting example, such as light from a torch or sun rays

questions.q: A triangle-shaped garden has corners K, L and M, with no three of them on one line, and a straight fence joins each pair of corners. (a) Write two names for the angle at corner L. (b) How many angles can be named using only the points K, L and M? Name them.
questions.a: (a) ∠KLM or ∠MLK. (b) Three angles, one at each corner: ∠KLM (at L), ∠LMK (at M) and ∠MKL (at K).
s: (a) Names the angle at L as ∠KLM or ∠MLK, with L as the middle letter
(b) States three angles and names one at each corner, with the vertex in the middle

questions.q: Say whether each of these gives the idea of a point, a line segment or a ray. (a) The tip of a nail (b) The edge of a ruler, from one end to the other (c) The light from a car's headlamp
questions.a: (a) A point. (b) A line segment. (c) A ray.
s: (a) Point
(b) Line segment
(c) Ray

questions.q: Raju draws the capital letter N with three straight strokes. The left stroke goes up from A to B, the slanting stroke goes down from B to C, and the right stroke goes up from C to D. (a) Name the angle formed at B, writing the vertex correctly. (b) Name the angle formed at C. (c) Raju writes the angle at B as ∠BAC. What is wrong with this name?
questions.a: (a) ∠ABC (or ∠CBA). (b) ∠BCD (or ∠DCB). (c) In ∠BAC the middle letter is A, so it names an angle with vertex A, not the angle at B. The vertex B must be the middle letter.
s: (a) Names the angle at B as ∠ABC or ∠CBA
(b) Names the angle at C as ∠BCD or ∠DCB
(c) Explains that the middle letter must be the vertex, so ∠BAC has vertex A, not B

questions.q: Seen from the side, an open laptop looks like an angle. The hinge is at the point H, the top edge of the screen is at the point S, and the front edge of the keyboard is at the point K. (a) Name this angle in two ways. (b) Name its vertex. (c) Name its two arms. (d) Meena pushes the screen further back. Does the angle become larger or smaller? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) ∠SHK or ∠KHS. (b) H, the hinge. (c) The rays HS and HK. (d) Larger, because the screen turns more about the hinge, and the size of an angle is the amount of turn about its vertex.
s: (a) Names the angle as ∠SHK or ∠KHS
(b) Names the vertex H
(c) Names the arms HS and HK
(d) Says larger, because the screen has turned more about the vertex

questions.q:
In a practice match the batter stands at point B. One fielder stands at point C in the covers and another at point M at mid-on. A ball hit from B rolls straight past C and stops at the boundary rope at point D, so B, C and D lie on one straight line. On his board the coach draws the direction from B through C and keeps it going past the rope to show the 'line of the shot'.
(a) Name the ray that the coach draws, and its starting point.
(b) Name the angle at the batter between the directions to the two fielders.
(c) Does the point D lie on the ray in (a)? Give a reason.
(d) The commentator calls the ball's actual path, from the bat to where it stopped, 'ray BC'. Is a ray the best name for that path, or is another figure better? Decide and justify.
questions.a: (a) Ray BC, with starting point B. (b) ∠CBM (or ∠MBC). (c) Yes. D is on the same straight line, beyond C, and ray BC starts at B and goes on endlessly through C, so it passes through D. (d) A ray is not the best name. The ball's path starts at B and stops at D, so it has two end points and is the line segment BD; a ray goes on endlessly, which the ball does not.
s: (a) Names ray BC with starting point B
(b) Names the angle ∠CBM with B as the middle letter
(c) Says yes, because D lies beyond C on the endless ray from B through C
(d) Decides the path is the line segment BD, because it has two end points, not a ray

questions.q: Rohan opens a garden gate a little, and then pushes it open much wider. Which statement about the angle between the gate and the wall is correct?
questions.a: It is larger the second time, because the gate has turned more about its hinge
o: It is larger the second time, because the gate has turned more about its hinge
It is larger the first time, because the gate is still close to the wall
It is the same both times, because the length of the gate has not changed
It cannot be compared without first measuring the length of the gate

questions.q: When two angles are compared by superimposition, what must be done first?
questions.a: Place one angle on the other with their vertices on top of each other
o: Place one angle on the other with their vertices on top of each other
Place the two angles side by side so that their arms touch
Draw both angles again so that all their arms are equally long
Cut both angles along their arms and lay the pieces in a row

questions.q: Leela traces the open mouths of a hippo, a crocodile and a dog from a nature film as angles. She superimposes them with the vertices together and the lower jaws along each other, and finds that the crocodile's upper jaw lies inside the hippo's angle, and the dog's upper jaw lies inside the crocodile's angle. Which order goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
questions.a: dog, crocodile, hippo
o: dog, crocodile, hippo
hippo, crocodile, dog
crocodile, dog, hippo
dog, hippo, crocodile

questions.q:
Assertion (A): As Arif opens the cover of his book further, the angle between the cover and the pages becomes larger.
Reason (R): The size of an angle is the amount of rotation about the vertex needed to move one arm onto the other.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: True or False: To compare two angles by superimposition, it is enough to lay one pair of arms along each other; the vertices need not be on top of each other. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. While superimposing, the vertices of the two angles must overlap and one pair of arms must lie along each other; only then does the position of the other arms show which angle is larger.
s: States False
Corrects it: the vertices must overlap as well as one pair of arms

questions.q: Rehan places ∠DEF on ∠GHK so that E lies on H and ray ED lies along ray HG. (a) If ray EF falls outside ∠GHK, which angle is larger? (b) If instead ray EF lies exactly along ray HK, what can he say about the two angles?
questions.a: (a) ∠DEF is larger, because its arm EF lies beyond HK, so more turn is needed from ED to EF than from HG to HK. (b) The two angles are equal in size, because their vertices and both pairs of arms lie on top of each other.
s: (a) Says ∠DEF is larger, because EF lies outside ∠GHK
(b) Says the angles are equal, because the vertices and both pairs of arms match

questions.q: In a drawing of a sunrise, five rays OA, OB, OC, OD and OE start from the centre O of the sun, in this order from left to right. (a) Which is larger, ∠AOE or ∠BOD? Give a reason. (b) Which is larger, ∠AOB or ∠AOD? Give a reason. (c) Can you tell reliably, just by looking at the drawing, whether ∠AOB is larger than ∠COD? What would you do to find out?
questions.a: (a) ∠AOE, because ∠BOD lies inside it: both OB and OD lie between OA and OE. (b) ∠AOD, because ∠AOB is a part of it (OB lies between OA and OD). (c) No. The two angles share no arm and neither lies inside the other, so they must be compared by superimposition, for example by tracing one and placing it on the other (or by using a transparent circle).
s: (a) Chooses ∠AOE, because ∠BOD lies inside it
(b) Chooses ∠AOD, because ∠AOB is a part of it
(c) Says looking is not reliable and names superimposition (or a transparent circle) as the way to compare

questions.q: Answer each part in one line. (a) Which two things are used to make a 'rotating arm'? (b) A rotating arm, shorter than the slit, is held over an angle-shaped slit. When does it pass through the slit? (c) The angle of a slit is greater than the angle of a rotating arm. Will the arm pass through the slit?
questions.a: (a) Two paper straws and a paper clip. (b) Only when the angle between its arms is equal to the angle of the slit. (c) No; it passes only if the two angles are equal.
s: (a) Names two paper straws and a paper clip
(b) Says the angle of the arms must equal the angle of the slit
(c) Says no, because the angles are not equal

questions.q: A folding paper fan has six ribs OA, OB, OC, OD, OE and OF fixed at a pin O, in this order. When it is opened, Gita checks by superimposition that every two neighbouring ribs make equal angles, so ∠AOB, ∠BOC, ∠COD, ∠DOE and ∠EOF are all equal. Call each of these angles one 'part'. (a) How many parts are there in ∠AOF? (b) Compare ∠AOC and ∠DOF. (c) Compare ∠BOE and ∠AOD. (d) Which is larger, ∠COF or ∠AOC, and by how many parts? (e) The rib OA is torn and is shorter than the rib OF. Gita's brother says this makes ∠AOB smaller than ∠EOF. Is he right? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 5 parts. (b) They are equal: each is 2 parts. (c) They are equal: each is 3 parts. (d) ∠COF is 3 parts and ∠AOC is 2 parts, so ∠COF is larger by 1 part. (e) No. The size of an angle depends on the amount of turn between its arms, not on how long the arms are, and the superimposition already showed the two angles are equal.
s: (a) Counts 5 parts in ∠AOF
(b) Shows ∠AOC and ∠DOF are both 2 parts, so equal
(c) Shows ∠BOE and ∠AOD are both 3 parts, so equal
(d) Finds ∠COF = 3 parts and ∠AOC = 2 parts, larger by 1 part
(e) Says no, because arm length does not change the size of an angle

questions.q:
A physiotherapist is helping Rehana straighten her elbow after an injury. Each week she traces the angle made at the elbow when Rehana opens her arm as far as she can, and then compares the tracings by superimposition. Her notes say: Week 2 on Week 1 - the forearm line of Week 2 falls outside the Week 1 angle. Week 3 on Week 2 - the forearm line of Week 3 falls inside the Week 2 angle. Week 4 on Week 2 - the forearm lines lie exactly on each other. The Week 2 tracing was drawn with lines twice as long as the Week 1 tracing.
(a) Before comparing, what must the physiotherapist put on top of each other, and what must lie along each other?
(b) Rehana says that the longer lines alone prove the Week 2 angle is larger than the Week 1 angle. Is she right?
(c) In which week or weeks was the opening widest?
(d) The report says, 'The opening grew every week.' Does the data support this? Justify.
questions.a: (a) The vertices (the elbow points) must lie on top of each other, and one pair of arms (the upper-arm lines) must lie along each other. (b) No. The length of the lines does not change an angle; Week 2 is larger than Week 1 only because its forearm line falls outside the Week 1 angle. (c) Weeks 2 and 4, which are equal: Week 2 is larger than Weeks 1 and 3, and Week 4 is equal to Week 2. (d) No. Week 3 was smaller than Week 2, and Week 4 only equalled Week 2, so the opening grew only from Week 1 to Week 2.
s: (a) States that the vertices must overlap and one pair of arms must lie along each other
(b) Says no, because arm length does not change the size of an angle
(c) Names Weeks 2 and 4 as the widest, equal to each other
(d) Decides the claim is not supported, citing the smaller Week 3 and the equal Week 4

questions.q: The lid of a tiffin box is opened through a half turn until it lies flat, in a straight line with the base. What is the angle between the lid and the base called?
questions.a: A straight angle
o: A straight angle
A right angle
An obtuse angle
An acute angle

questions.q: Which of these shows an acute angle?
questions.a: The tip of a sharpened pencil
o: The tip of a sharpened pencil
The corner of a notebook page
The hands of a clock at 6 o'clock
A door opened more than a quarter turn

questions.q:
Consider these statements.
I. An angle made by a turn of less than a half turn is always obtuse.
II. A straight angle contains exactly two right angles.
III. An obtuse angle is made by a turn of more than a quarter turn and less than a half turn.
Which of these statements are correct?
questions.a: II and III only
o: II and III only
I and II only
I and III only
All three

questions.q:
Match each object in Column I with the kind of angle it shows in Column II.
Column I: 1. The corner where a wall meets the floor  2. The two halves of a level see-saw plank on either side of its middle support  3. The tip of a sharpened pencil  4. A book cover opened more than a quarter turn but less than a half turn
Column II: A. Straight angle  B. Obtuse angle  C. Right angle  D. Acute angle
True or False: Any two lines that cross each other are perpendicular lines. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. Two lines are perpendicular only when they meet at a right angle; lines that cross at any other angle are not perpendicular.
s: States False
Corrects it: lines are perpendicular only when they meet at a right angle

questions.q: (a) When is an angle called a right angle? (b) Give one example of a right angle in your classroom.
questions.a: (a) An angle is a right angle when it is exactly half of a straight angle, that is, a quarter turn. (b) For example, a corner of a window, of the door frame or of the blackboard.
s: (a) Says a right angle is exactly half of a straight angle (a quarter turn)
(b) Gives a fitting classroom example, such as a window corner

questions.q: Asha stands facing North. Classify the angle she turns through in each case as acute, right or obtuse, and give a reason using a quarter turn or a half turn. (a) She turns clockwise until she faces East. (b) She turns clockwise until she faces North-East, which is halfway between North and East. (c) She turns clockwise until she faces South-East, which is halfway between East and South.
questions.a: (a) A right angle: turning from North to East is exactly a quarter turn. (b) Acute: North to North-East is half of a quarter turn, which is less than a quarter turn. (c) Obtuse: North to South-East is a quarter turn and then half of another quarter turn, which is more than a quarter turn but less than the half turn to South.
s: (a) Right angle, because North to East is a quarter turn
(b) Acute, because the turn is less than a quarter turn
(c) Obtuse, because the turn is more than a quarter turn but less than a half turn

questions.q: Sameer marks a point O on the straight edge of a sheet of paper, so that the edge on the two sides of O forms ∠AOB. He folds the sheet through O so that OB falls exactly on OA, and then opens it to see a crease OC. (a) What kind of angle is ∠AOB? (b) Explain why ∠AOC and ∠COB are equal. (c) What is each of these two angles called, and what are the crease and the edge called when they meet like this?
questions.a: (a) A straight angle, since its arms OA and OB lie in a straight line. (b) When folded, OB fell exactly on OA with the crease OC common to both, so one angle lay exactly on the other (superimposition by folding); hence they are equal. (c) Each is a right angle, and the crease and the edge are perpendicular lines.
s: (a) Says ∠AOB is a straight angle because its arms lie in a straight line
(b) Explains equality by the fold placing one angle exactly on the other
(c) Names them right angles and the crease and edge perpendicular lines

questions.q: Points A, O and B lie on a straight line with O between A and B. Two rays OC and OD are drawn on the same side of the line, so that the rays come in the order OA, OC, OD, OB as you turn from OA to OB. ∠AOC is exactly a right angle. Without measuring, classify each angle and give a reason. (a) ∠AOB (b) ∠COB (c) ∠AOD (d) ∠DOB
questions.a: (a) A straight angle: OA and OB lie in a straight line (a half turn). (b) A right angle: the straight angle AOB contains two right angles and ∠AOC is one of them, so ∠COB is the other. (c) Obtuse: OD lies between OC and OB, so ∠AOD is more than the right angle AOC but less than the straight angle AOB. (d) Acute: ∠DOB is a part of the right angle COB, so it is less than a right angle.
s: (a) Straight angle, because OA and OB lie in a straight line
(b) Right angle, because a straight angle holds two right angles and ∠AOC is one
(c) Obtuse, because ∠AOD is more than ∠AOC and less than ∠AOB
(d) Acute, because ∠DOB is part of the right angle COB

questions.q:
Rafi, a carpenter, is building a bookshelf. To check each corner he uses a postcard, whose corner is a right angle. He puts the corner of the card into each corner of the shelf, with one edge of the card along one side of the shelf. At corner P, the other edge of the card lies exactly along the other side of the shelf. At corner Q, the other side of the shelf lies outside the card's corner, though the shelf there is far from flat. At corner R, the other side of the shelf lies inside the card's corner.
(a) What kind of angle is corner P?
(b) What kind of angle is corner Q? Give a reason.
(c) What kind of angle is corner R? Give a reason.
(d) Rafi's helper checks corner S with a postcard whose corner got bent, and the card fits exactly. Can Rafi trust that corner S is a right angle? Justify.
questions.a: (a) A right angle. (b) Obtuse: it is larger than a right angle but, not being flat, less than a straight angle. (c) Acute: it is smaller than a right angle. (d) No. The check works only if the card's corner is exactly a right angle. With a bent corner, an exact fit shows only that S equals the bent corner, which may not be a right angle.
s: (a) Says corner P is a right angle
(b) Says corner Q is obtuse: more than a right angle, less than a straight angle
(c) Says corner R is acute: less than a right angle
(d) Decides no, because the test needs a card corner that is exactly a right angle

questions.q: How many degrees does one full turn measure?
Mehul counts the 1° units between the arms of an angle on an unlabelled protractor and finds 75 of them. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The angle measures 75° and is smaller than a right angle
o: The angle measures 75° and is smaller than a right angle
The angle measures 75° and is larger than a right angle
The angle measures 105° and is larger than a right angle
The angle measures 15° and is smaller than a right angle

questions.q: An unlabelled protractor has a long mark for every 10°, counting from the 0 mark at the right end, and a medium mark 5° after each long mark. The vertex of an angle is at the centre and one arm passes through the 0 mark. Tanu moves along the edge from the 0 mark. Not counting the 0 mark itself, she passes 8 long marks and then stops at the next medium mark, where the other arm crosses. What does the angle measure?

Consider these statements about why a full turn is divided into 360°.
I. The Rigveda speaks of a wheel with 360 spokes.
II. 360 can be divided evenly by 12, the number of months in a year, and by 24, the number of hours in a day.
III. 360 can be divided evenly by every number from 1 to 10.
Which of these statements are correct?
questions.a: I and II only
o: I and II only
I and III only
II and III only
All three

questions.q: (a) Write the degree measure of a full turn. (b) Use it to find the degree measure of a quarter turn.
questions.a: (a) 360°. (b) A quarter turn is 1/4 of 360°, which is 90°.
s: (a) Writes 360° for a full turn

questions.q: A round flower bed is divided from its centre into 9 equal sections. (a) Find the angle at the centre of each section. (b) Three neighbouring sections are planted with marigolds. Find the angle at the centre of the marigold part.
s: (a) Divides the full turn: 360° / 9 = 40°

questions.q: Ravi measures ∠PQR = 110°. He draws a ray QS inside the angle so that ∠PQS = 50°, and says that QS is the angle bisector of ∠PQR. (a) Find ∠SQR. (b) Is Ravi right? Give a reason. (c) What should ∠PQS measure for QS to be the bisector?
questions.a: (a) ∠SQR = 110° - 50° = 60°. (b) No. A bisector divides an angle into two equal angles, but 50° and 60° are not equal. (c) Half of 110°, which is 55°.
s: (a) Finds ∠SQR = 60°
(b) Says no, because the two parts 50° and 60° are not equal
(c) Finds half of 110° = 55°

questions.q: A rangoli artist makes round stencils, each divided from its centre into equal sections. Find the angle at the centre of one section when a stencil is divided into (a) 2 equal sections (b) 4 equal sections (c) 5 equal sections (d) 10 equal sections (e) 12 equal sections.
s: (a) Finds 180°
(b) Finds 90°
(c) Finds 72°
(d) Finds 36°
(e) Finds 30°

questions.q: Five rays OA, OB, OC, OD and OE start from a point O. A protractor is placed with its centre on O, and on its outer scale the rays pass through these marks: OA at 0, OB at 35, OC at 70, OD at 125 and OE at 180. (a) Find ∠AOC and ∠BOD. (b) Which of the two angles in (a) is a right angle? (c) Find ∠COD and ∠DOE, and say which ray bisects ∠COE. (d) Does OC bisect ∠BOD? Show why or why not. (e) Which ray bisects ∠AOC? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) ∠AOC = 70° - 0° = 70° and ∠BOD = 125° - 35° = 90°. (b) ∠BOD. (c) ∠COD = 125° - 70° = 55° and ∠DOE = 180° - 125° = 55°, so OD bisects ∠COE. (d) No: ∠BOC = 70° - 35° = 35° but ∠COD = 55°, which are not equal. (e) OB, because ∠AOB = 35° and ∠BOC = 35° are equal.
s: (a) Finds ∠AOC = 70° and ∠BOD = 90° by subtracting scale readings
(b) Picks ∠BOD as the right angle
(c) Finds ∠COD = ∠DOE = 55° and names OD as the bisector of ∠COE
(d) Shows ∠BOC = 35° and ∠COD = 55° are unequal, so OC is not the bisector
(e) Names OB, since ∠AOB = ∠BOC = 35°

questions.q:
In a maths lab, four students measure the same angle PQR with the same semicircular protractor. The protractor has an outer scale and an inner scale, and at every mark the two numbers add up to 180. Here is how each of them worked.
Asha: centre on Q, QR along the 0 of the outer scale; QP crosses 68 on the outer scale; she writes 68°.
Bilal: placed exactly like Asha, but he reads QP on the inner scale and writes 112°.
Charu: centre on Q, but QR lies along the 10 mark of the outer scale; QP crosses 78 on the same scale; she writes 78°.
Dev: puts the centre on P instead of Q and writes 50°.
(a) Whose method is fully correct?
(b) What should Charu have written? Show the working.
(c) Explain Bilal's mistake and correct his reading.
(d) The teacher says, 'Once corrected, three of the four readings agree.' Is she right? Whose reading cannot be corrected, and why?
questions.a: (a) Asha's. (b) Her arms are at 10 and 78 on the same scale, so the angle is 78° - 10° = 68°. (c) QR was on the 0 of the outer scale, so he should read the outer scale. The inner reading 112 sits at the outer reading 180 - 112 = 68, so the angle is 68°. (d) Yes. Asha, Bilal and Charu all give 68° once corrected. Dev's reading cannot be corrected, because the centre was not on the vertex Q, so it does not measure ∠PQR at all.
s: (a) Names Asha
(b) Finds 78° - 10° = 68° for Charu
(c) Explains he used the wrong scale and corrects 112° to 180° - 112° = 68°
(d) Agrees with the teacher and explains that Dev's centre was not on the vertex

questions.q: True or False: Every reflex angle is larger than every obtuse angle. Give the reason.
questions.a: True. Every obtuse angle is less than 180°, and every reflex angle is more than 180°, so any reflex angle is larger than any obtuse angle.
s: States True
Gives the reason: obtuse angles are below 180° and reflex angles are above 180°

questions.q: Shreya draws the capital letter V so that its two strokes meet at the bottom at an angle of 50°. (a) What kind of angle is this? (b) She wants the opening to be exactly a right angle. By how many degrees must she widen it?
questions.a: (a) Acute, since 50° is more than 0° and less than 90°. (b) 90° - 50° = 40°.
s: (a) Classifies 50° as acute

questions.q: An angle measures a whole number of degrees, x. When x is doubled, the result is a reflex angle. When x is halved, the result is an acute angle. (a) Give one possible value of x and check both conditions. (b) What kind of angle must x itself be? Explain. (c) Can x be 90°? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) For example, x = 100°: 2 x 100° = 200°, which is between 180° and 360°, so it is reflex; 100° / 2 = 50°, which is acute. (b) Obtuse. For 2x to be more than 180°, x must be more than 90°, and for 2x to be less than 360°, x must be less than 180°. (c) No. 2 x 90° = 180°, which is a straight angle, not a reflex angle.
s: (a) Gives a value from 91° to 179° and checks that its double is reflex and its half is acute
(b) Reasons that x is more than 90° and less than 180°, so x is obtuse
(c) Says no, because double 90° is 180°, a straight angle

questions.q: The 12 numbers on a clock face are equally spaced around a full turn, and at each whole hour the minute hand points to 12. (a) Find the angle between two neighbouring numbers. (b) Find the smaller angle between the hands at 5 o'clock and classify it. (c) Find the smaller angle between the hands at 11 o'clock and classify it. (d) List every whole hour from 1 o'clock to 11 o'clock at which the smaller angle between the hands is obtuse.
questions.a: (a) 360° / 12 = 30°. (b) The hands are 5 numbers apart: 5 x 30° = 150°, an obtuse angle. (c) Going the shorter way, the hands are 1 number apart: 30°, an acute angle. (d) 4, 5, 7 and 8 o'clock, where the smaller angles are 120°, 150°, 150° and 120°.
s: (b) Finds 150° at 5 o'clock and calls it obtuse
(c) Finds 30° at 11 o'clock and calls it acute
(d) Lists 4, 5, 7 and 8 o'clock

questions.q: A furniture shop sells a reclining chair whose back can be locked at five positions. The angle between the seat and the back is 95°, 110°, 125°, 160° or 180°. A doctor tells Mr Rao that for reading the angle must be obtuse but not more than 120°, and that for resting flat it must be a straight angle. (a) Classify each of the five angles. (b) Which positions can Mr Rao use for reading? (c) Which position can he use for resting flat? (d) Through how many degrees does the back turn when he moves it from the 110° position to the flat position? (e) His daughter finds another chair whose back locks only at 100°, 115° and 150°. Which chair suits both of the doctor's instructions? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 95°, 110°, 125° and 160° are obtuse angles; 180° is a straight angle. (b) 95° and 110°, which are obtuse and not more than 120°. (c) The 180° position. (d) 180° - 110° = 70°. (e) The first chair. The second chair has reading positions (100° and 115°) but no 180° position, so it cannot be used for resting flat, while the first chair meets both instructions.
s: (a) Classifies 95°, 110°, 125°, 160° as obtuse and 180° as straight
(b) Picks 95° and 110° for reading
(c) Picks the 180° position for resting flat
(e) Chooses the first chair, because the second has no straight-angle position

questions.q:
A school fixes a security camera at the corner O of its boundary wall. The wall runs along the ray OW, and the camera's turn is measured in degrees from OW. The gate is seen at 60° from OW, the bicycle stand at 150°, and the far end of a straight fence, which is in line with the wall on the other side of O, at 180°. Two camera models cost the same: Model X can point in any direction from 0° to 135°, and Model Y in any direction from 45° to 180°.
(a) What kind of angle does the direction of the bicycle stand make with OW?
(b) Through how many degrees must a camera turn from the gate to the bicycle stand? What kind of angle is this?
(c) What kind of angle is formed between OW and the direction of the far end of the fence?
(d) The school needs one camera that can see both the gate and the bicycle stand. Which model should it buy? Justify.
questions.a: (a) An obtuse angle, since 150° is more than 90° and less than 180°. (b) 150° - 60° = 90°, a right angle. (c) A straight angle (180°). (d) Model Y. It covers 45° to 180°, which includes both 60° and 150°, while Model X stops at 135° and so cannot see the bicycle stand at 150°.
s: (a) Classifies 150° as obtuse
(b) Finds 150° - 60° = 90°, a right angle
(c) Names it a straight angle
(d) Chooses Model Y, checking that 60° and 150° both lie in its range and 150° is beyond Model X
